title: 1 · Java Platform & Types (Deep Dive)
learn:
The story: a universal translator

Imagine writing a speech once and having it understood in every country, because a translator in each country knows one shared “travel language”. That is Java. You write source code (.java). The compiler javac turns it into bytecode (.class), the shared travel language. Each computer has a JVM that reads bytecode and runs it. Hence “write once, run anywhere”: platform independent.

JDK vs JRE vs JVM

Think of a restaurant. The JDK (Development Kit) is the whole kitchen: compiler plus tools, needed to write Java. The JRE (Runtime Environment) holds the libraries a program needs to run, enough for a diner to eat. The JVM (Virtual Machine) is the chef who executes the bytecode: class loader plus execution engine. Exam answer: three stages = write source, compile to bytecode, JVM executes. Always draw the arrows.

Why Java is popular

Platform independent, object-oriented, strongly and statically typed (every variable has a declared type checked before running), automatic memory management (the garbage collector frees unused objects), robust, and multi-threaded (several tasks at once).

Variables: labelled boxes

A variable is a named box. The type decides the box size and what fits inside. Declare it, then assign it: int age = 21;

The 8 primitives

Whole numbers grow: byte 8 bits (-128 to 127), short 16, int 32 (about ±2.1 billion), long 64 (needs an L: 8000000000L). Decimals: float 32 bits (6-7 digits, needs an f: 3.14f) and double 64 bits (about 15 digits, the default). char is one character in single quotes ('A'), 16 bits. boolean is only true or false. A String is not a primitive, it uses double quotes.

Primitive vs reference

A primitive box holds the value itself and can never be null. A reference box holds an address pointing to an object on the heap (String, arrays, your classes) and can be null. Calling a method on null causes the famous NullPointerException.

Casting and overflow

Small to big is automatic (int to double). Big to small needs a cast and loses data: int x = (int) 3.99; gives 3 (it truncates, it does not round). Integer division chops decimals: 7 / 2 is 3, while 7 / 2.0 is 3.5. % is the remainder (7 % 2 is 1; n % 2 == 0 tests even).

Names and style

Rules (compile errors if broken): letters, digits, _ and $, cannot start with a digit, no reserved words, case-sensitive. Conventions: camelCase for variables and methods, PascalCase for classes, SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE for constants declared with final.

Basic syntax

Statements end with ;. Blocks use { }. The file name must match the public class name. Comments: // line and /* block */. The entry point is public static void main(String[] args).
